answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with pulse-dispersed echo attestation. After a task, peers publish an echo confirming it, but credit arrives only when echoes span at least three pulse windows, not one burst. Fake identities echo together, instantly and identically, while genuine peers reply at scattered times. A cluster whose echoes collapse into one pulse counts as one voice, its credit shared to near zero, and its members fall to nadir status, rebuilding slowly through supervised low-value work. Honest agents pay nothing extra, yet mass duplication becomes costly and visible.
